The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety and effectiveness of berobenatide in adults with overweight or obesity who have already lost weight while taking semaglutide or tirzepatide. The study does not include people with diabetes.

Participants will be in the study for about 11 months.

* evaluate the safety, tolerability, efficacy, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of single ascending doses of ALN-2232 in patients with obesity
* evaluate the safety, tolerability, efficacy, PK, and PD of multiple doses of ALN-2232 in patients with obesity
* evaluate the safety, tolerability, efficacy, PK, and PD of multiple doses of ALN-2232 co-initiated with tirzepatide in patients with obesity

trials.title: Subcutaneous Tirzepatide Once-weekly in Patients With Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis (STOP KNEE-OA)
trials.summary: This is a trial of tirzepatide in people with obesity and knee osteoarthritis. The main purpose of this study is to see if tirzepatide can reduce number of these participants who require a knee replacement. Participants will be randomized to take a weekly injection of tirzepatide or a placebo for a total of 72 weeks.

Participants will either get semaglutide or a dummy medicine - which treatment participants get is decided by chance.

trials.title: Tirzepatide s Dopaminergic Effects in Alcohol Use Disorders (AUD)
trials.summary:
Background:

Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) agonist drugs are used to treat diabetes and aid weight loss. They may also help reduce cravings for drugs and alcohol. Researchers want to know if a GLP-1 drug (tirzepatide) can lessen the urge to drink in people with alcohol use disorder (AUD).

Objective:

To learn how the brains of people with AUD respond to a GLP-1 drug.

Eligibility:

People aged 21 to 65 years with AUD who are non-treatment seeking. They must be enrolled in protocol 14-AA-0181.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether continuous glucose monitoring using FreeStyle Libre 3 will improve HbA1c compared to SMBG over 16 weeks in adults with sub-optimally controlled (HbA1c 7.5-11%) Type 2 diabetes on basal therapy.

trials.summary: The is a pilot, 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial of individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD) newly initiating buprenorphine to receive either weekly injections of semaglutide (n=23) or matching placebo (n=23). The primary aim is to determine the effects of semaglutide on cue-reactivity among individuals with OUD. The secondary aim is to assess the preliminary efficacy, safety, and tolerability of semaglutide for OUD.

trials.summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate how GLP-1 receptor analogs, such as semaglutide (Wegovy®), influence processes that determine eating behavior, binge eating, and weight regulation via the gut-brain axis. The main question it aims to answer is: to identify for whom semaglutide works best.

Participants will:

* undergo a semaglutide treatment for 6 months
* visit the clinic for 2-4 study checkup and tests
* wear a smartwatch and complete questionnaires on their smartphone

The aim is to compare BGM0504 Injection 15 mg with semaglutide 1.0 mg in Chinese T2DM patients with obesity and inadequate control despite diet and exercise. Over 52 weeks of once weekly treatment, efficacy and safety are evaluated, including the rate of diabetes remission at 12 weeks after treatment discontinuation.

Participation in the study will last about 9 months.

trials.title: Mirikizumab Administered at the Same Time as Tirzepatide in Adult Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis and Obesity or Overweight: Phase 3b Study
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study is to show whether in these individuals, treatment with both mirikizumab and tirzepatide, compared with treatment with mirikizumab and placebo, leads to decrease or disappearance of UC symptoms, and loss of at least one-tenth of the overall body weight.

Participation in this study will last up to 61 weeks, including 52 weeks of treatment.

trials.title: A Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) on the Reduction on Morbidity and Mortality in Adults With Obesity
trials.summary: This study will investigate the effect of tirzepatide on the reduction of morbidity and mortality in adults living with obesity and provide additional evidence for the potential clinical benefits of tirzepatide in this population.

trials.title: Insulin and Insulin Pulses During Fasting
trials.summary: Fasting hyperglycemia contributes disproportionately to nonenzymatic glycosylation and the microvascular complications of type 2 diabetes. However, little is known about the regulation of glucose concentrations in the fasting state relative to what is known about the postprandial state. The proposed experiment is part of a series of experiments designed to establish how glucagon and insulin interact with their receptors to control fasting glucose in health and in prediabetes.

trials.title: Mirikizumab and Tirzepatide Administered in Adult Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease and Obesity or Overweight
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab and concomitantly administered tirzepatide in adult participants with moderately to severely active CD and obesity, or overweight.

The maximum duration of this study is up to 61 weeks.

trials.title: A Research Study to Look at How Semaglutide Compared to Placebo Affects Diabetic Eye Disease in People With Type 2 Diabetes
trials.summary: This study will look at the long-term effects of semaglutide (active medicine) on diabetic eye disease when compared to placebo (dummy medicine). The study will be performed in people with type 2 diabetes. Participants will either get semaglutide or placebo in addition to their diabetes medicines - which treatment the participant gets is decided by chance. trials.title: The Effect of Tirzepatide on Menopausal Vasomotor Symptoms and Biological Aging in Post-menopausal Women With Obesity
trials.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the effect of tirzepatide on vasomotor symptoms and on measures of biological aging.

trials.title: Imaging in Semaglutide Study
trials.summary: In this preliminary observation study, the investigators will assess muscle function in terms of muscle strength and leverage imaging (MRI) and spectroscopy (31P-MRS) based techniques to assess longitudinal changes in muscle volume, quality and metabolic function in patients with T2D and obesity prescribed to semaglutide therapy. trials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ribupatide Administered Once Weekly in Participants Living With Obesity or Overweight and Diabetes
trials.summary:
The primary objective of this study is to demonstrate that ribupatide (KAI-9531) subcutaneous (SC) injection once weekly is superior to placebo on:

* Percent change in body weight
* Change in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)

trials.title: A Study to Evaluate the Effect of Retatrutide on Insulin Secretion and Insulin Sensitivity in Adult Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
trials.summary: The primary objective of Study GZQG is to compare the effect of retatrutide and placebo on total clamp disposition index (cDI) after 28 weeks of treatment.

trials.title: Multi-peptide Vaccination and Bispecific PSMAxCD3 Antibody Treatment in Patients With Prostate Cancer
trials.summary: This trial is a phase II, randomized, open label study designed to evaluate safety, tolerability and efficacy of CC-1, a bispecific antibody (bsAb) with PSMAxCD3 specificity, and of VACXS15-PC01, a prostate cancer (PC)-specific multi-peptide vaccine, both administered as single agent or in combination to patients affected with biochemical recurrence (BCR) of PC after local therapy with curative intent. Patients will not receive other treatments during trial participation.

trials.title: Efficacy and Safety of a Drinkable Nutraceutical for Hair Loss in Patients Using GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonists
trials.summary: The purpose of this clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy of Olistic© Next Women, a nutraceutical supplement, compared with placebo in improving hair loss in patients undergoing treatment with GLP-1/GIP agonists. This 6-month, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical study investigates whether daily supplementation with Olistic© Next Women leads to significant improvements in hair loss in this patient population. trials.title: Study of Patients Being Treated With Anti-obesity Medication
trials.summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the real-world effects of selected obesity medications in adults undergoing medical weight management. The main outcomes of interest are changes in body composition, routine clinical markers, muscular performance, and nutritional intake over the course of treatment. Additionally, the influence of lifestyle factors on changes in these outcome variables will be examined.

trials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ribupatide in Participants Living With Obesity or Overweight With Weight-Related Comorbidities Who Do Not Have Diabetes
trials.summary: The primary objective of the study is to determine the effects of ribupatide (KAI-9531) subcutaneous (SC) injection once weekly compared to placebo on percent change in body weight.

trials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ribupatide Administered Once Weekly Compared With Semaglutide and Placebo in Participants Living With Obesity Who Do Not Have Diabetes
trials.summary: The primary objective of this study is to demonstrate that ribupatide (KAI-9531) subcutaneous (SC) injection once weekly is superior to semaglutide SC once weekly and to placebo SC once weekly on percent change in body weight.

trials.title: The Role of Glucagon in Glucose Metabolism in Humans With and Without Bariatric Surgery
trials.summary: The goal of this study is to understand the role of glucagon signal on glucose metabolism in individuals with and without bariatric surgery. The study is involved with measuring glucose metabolism with glucagon infusion and glucagon receptor blockade. We use an investigational drug called REMD 477. "Investigational" means that the has not yet been approved by the U.S. Food \& Drug Administration (FDA). trials.title: Glycemic and Weight Loss Effects of GLP-1R Agonist Therapy in Subjects With Spinal Cord Injury and Type 2 Diabetes
trials.summary: It is not known whether a new diabetes drug, semaglutide, is an effective treatment for type 2 diabetes for persons with spinal cord injury (SCI), a population at higher risk for this condition. Therefore, this study looks at the effect of semaglutide on glucose levels in the body and other information about type 2 diabetes and obesity.

trials.title: The Chronic Kidney Disease Adaptive Platform Trial Investigating Various Agents for Therapeutic Effect
trials.summary:
CAPTIVATE is an international, multi-centre, Phase III, adaptive, platform, randomised controlled trial in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

CAPTIVATE aims to find the best treatment, or combination of treatments, that slow the progression of CKD so that fewer people develop kidney failure.

CAPTIVATE provides a research platform that allows many treatment-related questions to be answered within a common trial set-up.

trials.title: The Effect of Oral Semaglutide on Bone Turnover in Patients With T2D: a Randomized Placebo-controlled Clinical Trial
trials.summary: The hypothesis for this study is that oral Semaglutide, a GLP-1Ra, has a positive effect on the balance between build-up and degradation as well as the strength of the bones in men and women aged 50-85 years with type 2 diabetes and an increased risk of bone fractures. Treatment involves once daily oral GLP-1Ra semaglutide or matching placebo for 52 weeks. trials.title: Effect of Prolonged Fasting Time on Gastric Residual Volume in Patients Taking GLP1 Receptor Agonists
trials.summary: The aim of this study is to determine whether a modified fasting protocol can reduce the potential risk of aspiration for patients currently prescribed GLP1-RAs.

trials.title: Weight-loss Drug for Fertility-Sparing Treatment of Atypical Hyperplasia and Low-grade Cancer of the Endometrium
trials.summary: The incidence of endometrial cancer is increasing at an alarming rate. This trend parallels the rising rate of obesity, the most significant risk factor for endometrial cancer. Young women with obesity and endometrial cancer or atypical hyperplasia who want to maintain their fertility are treated with progestin therapy, such as progestin intra-uterine device (pIUD), which is associated with a mediocre response rate and high recurrence rate, and does not address the underlying cause, obesity. trials.title: Lu-177-DOTATATE (Lutathera) in Combination With Olaparib in Inoperable Gastroenteropancreatico Neuroendocrine Tumors (GEP-NET)
trials.summary:
Background:

A neuroendocrine tumor is a rare type of tumor. It comes from body cells called neuroendocrine cells. Sometimes, these tumors develop in the gastrointestinal tract and pancreas. Researchers want to find out if a combination of drugs can shrink these tumors.

Objective:

To learn if people with certain neuroendocrine tumors can take a combination of 2 drugs, Lutathera and Olaparib, without having severe side effects, and if this treatment makes the tumors shrink.

trials.title: Tirzepatide in Obesity-Driven Endometrial Cancer
trials.summary:
LCCC2415 examines the antiproliferative effect of tirzepatide on the endometrium of endometrial cancer (EC). This is a pre-operative window clinical study. Endometrial biopsy samples from patients before tirzepatide treatment will be compared to their post-intervention hysterectomy specimens. If archival tissue is unavailable, a fresh biopsy will be taken before tirzepatide treatment. Post-intervention tissue will be collected from the hysterectomy specimen.

archive.title: ADA: Boehringer touts survodutide weight loss as tolerability questions linger
archive.summary: At ADA 2026, Boehringer Ingelheim presented phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE data for its glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist survodutide, reporting up to 16.6% average weight loss and large visceral-fat reductions. Coverage noted higher treatment-discontinuation rates on the highest doses than for some competing GLP-1 drugs.

archive.title: GLP-1 Drugs 2026: ADA Sessions Close as New Standards End Single-Goal Diabetes Care
archive.summary: A wrap-up of the American Diabetes Association's 2026 Scientific Sessions, where new treatment standards elevated cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction alongside blood-sugar control. The meeting featured phase 3 data for retatrutide, orforglipron and other agents.

archive.title: Ultra-long-acting GLP-1 improves weight loss with and without type 2 diabetes
archive.summary: Data presented at ADA 2026 on berobenatide, an investigational ultra-long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist studied in the VESPER phase 2b program, reported meaningful weight loss in people with obesity or overweight. Its extended half-life points to potential monthly dosing.

archive.title: Rivus Announces Preclinical Data for RV-8451, a Muscle-Preserving Oral GLP-1, at ADA 2026
archive.summary: Rivus Pharmaceuticals reported preclinical results for RV-8451, an experimental oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, describing fat loss with preservation of lean muscle in non-human primate studies. The company said it plans to file an IND application in early 2027.

archive.title: What RFK Jr.'s Peptide Reclassification Actually Means: A Pharmacist's Take
archive.summary: A pharmacist explains the February 2026 HHS announcement that roughly 14 of 19 FDA-restricted peptides would move from Category 2 to Category 1, restoring a legal compounding pathway with a prescription. The article stresses that reclassification is not FDA approval and does not establish safety or efficacy.

archive.title: Novo Nordisk Advances Cardiometabolic Pipeline with CagriSema and Zenagamtide Data at ADA 2026
archive.summary: Novo Nordisk previewed roughly 40 abstracts for ADA 2026, including new CagriSema data on glycemic control and weight loss and mid-stage results for zenagamtide (amycretin). The release outlined the company's broader cardiometabolic pipeline.

archive.title: Next-Gen Weight-Loss Drug Retatrutide Moves a Step Closer to FDA Approval
archive.summary: Eli Lilly's triple-receptor agonist retatrutide, which targets GLP-1, GIP and glucagon, showed participants losing roughly 28% of body weight over 80 weeks in the phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. The results position it as potentially more potent than current single- and dual-agonist obesity drugs.

archive.title: FDA Proposes Ban on Bulk Compounding of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide
archive.summary: The FDA announced on April 30, 2026 that it is proposing to exclude semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list, citing no current clinical need for outsourcing facilities to compound them from bulk substances. A public comment period was opened ahead of a final decision.

archive.title: FDA Mulls Compounding for Peptides Previously Flagged Over Safety Risks
archive.summary: The FDA scheduled a July 2026 advisory-committee meeting to reconsider whether compounding pharmacies may prepare seven peptides the agency had earlier flagged for safety concerns. The piece notes HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s support for broader peptide access.

archive.title: FDA Considers Adding a Dozen Peptides to Its Bulk Drug Compounding List
archive.summary: The Regulatory Affairs Professionals Society reported that the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee will evaluate whether about twelve peptides should be added to the Section 503A bulk drug list for licensed compounding. Proposed indications include wound healing, insomnia and ulcerative colitis.

archive.title: FDA Approves Orforglipron, First GLP-1 Pill Without Time, Food, or Water Restrictions
archive.summary: The FDA approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron (Foundayo), an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, for adults with obesity or overweight, with no food, water or timing restrictions. Trials reported dose-dependent weight loss versus placebo.

archive.title: Tirzepatide Cuts Major Heart and Kidney Risks in New SURPASS-CVOT Data
archive.summary: In the SURPASS-CVOT trial in people with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, tirzepatide met noninferiority versus dulaglutide on the primary cardiovascular endpoint and showed reductions in a broader cardiorenal composite. Gastrointestinal side effects were more common with tirzepatide.

archive.title: Semaglutide Does Not Slow Alzheimer's Disease, Two Clinical Trials Find
archive.summary: Two phase 3 trials (EVOKE and EVOKE+) of about 3,800 patients with early Alzheimer's found that oral semaglutide produced no significant difference in disease progression versus placebo over two years. Some biomarker changes in a subgroup did not translate into slower cognitive decline.

archive.title: Novo Nordisk Expands Pivotal Amycretin Program After Dual Agonist Shines in Diabetes
archive.summary: Novo Nordisk said it would expand the phase 3 program for amycretin, a single-molecule GLP-1/amylin co-agonist, after phase 2 diabetes data showed substantial HbA1c and body-weight reductions. The move advances amycretin alongside the company's CagriSema program.

archive.title: Semaglutide Receives FDA Approval for Treatment of MASH
archive.summary: The FDA approved semaglutide (Wegovy) 2.4 mg as the first GLP-1 receptor agonist for non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis, based on the ESSENCE trial. Reported data showed higher rates of MASH resolution versus placebo.

archive.title: FDA Approval for Mitochondrial Therapeutic Elamipretide, Formerly SS-31
archive.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval to elamipretide (FORZINITY), the mitochondria-targeted peptide previously known as SS-31, for Barth syndrome, a rare mitochondrial disease. The approval was supported by trial data showing improved muscle strength.
